content.summary: Welcome to the final reading module of level B1. Here, we bridge the gap into B2 by examining how fluent speakers organize extended debates, construct solid arguments, and manage counterarguments in written texts.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Complex sentence structures using contrastive and causal conjunctions.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Discourse markers such as furthermore, nevertheless, and consequently.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Identifying paragraph functions, tracking logical chains, and evaluating argumentative evidence.

learningObjectives: Understand the main structure of an advanced B2 argument text.
Recognize transition signals used to link complex ideas in formal writing.
Analyze how authors introduce and refute opposing viewpoints.

contextWarmup.prompt: When someone disagrees with your opinion in a discussion, what is the best strategy to respond?
options: Acknowledge their point politely before presenting counter-evidence.
Shout loudly until they agree with your initial statement.
Change the topic immediately to avoid conflict.
contextWarmup.explanation: Acknowledging opposing views before refuting them demonstrates maturity and strong argumentative structure, which is essential for B2 proficiency.

rules: Opening Statement Structure: Start with a clear thesis plus a preview of your main points.
PEE Framework: Point (state your argument) + Evidence (provide facts or examples) + Explanation (connect evidence to your point).
Discourse Markers for Coherence: Use transition words effectively to guide the reader through your logical reasoning.
Addressing Counterarguments: Always acknowledge opposing views honestly before providing your refutation.

commonTrap.explanation: Many learners think a good argument only talks about why they are right. In academic and B2 discussions, ignoring counterarguments makes your text weak.
commonTrap.wrong: My idea is the only correct one and nobody can say otherwise.
commonTrap.correct: While some people argue that costs are too high, the long-term benefits clearly outweigh the expenses.

content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how subjects and verbs smoothly merge in everyday discussions:

contractions.subject: It
contractions.exampleFull: It is clear that the policy works.
contractions.exampleContracted: It's clear that the policy works.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Discourse Markers
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice argumentative transitions:

items.exampleSentence: Furthermore, the research indicates that regular exercise improves mental health significantly.
The plan has some drawbacks. Nevertheless, I believe we should proceed with caution.
The city failed to invest in public transport; consequently, traffic congestion worsened dramatically.
A common counterargument is that technology reduces face-to-face communication skills.
She presented compelling evidence that supports her position on climate change.
I acknowledge that there are valid concerns, but the benefits outweigh the risks.
The speaker attempted to refute the opposition's claims with statistical data.
Academic discourse requires clear structure and evidence-based reasoning.
In your conclusion, synthesize the main arguments to show how they connect.
I strongly advocate for increased funding in education to ensure equal opportunities.

content.passageTitle: The Art of Structured Debate in Modern Society
paragraphs: Engaging in public discourse requires more than just holding a strong opinion. When preparing for a debate, speakers must present a clear thesis statement supported by compelling evidence. Furthermore, organizing your thoughts using the point, evidence, and explanation framework helps your audience follow your reasoning without confusion.

Nevertheless, every strong argument faces potential criticism. A skilled debater must acknowledge opposing viewpoints and be ready to refute them with reliable facts. Consequently, mastering argument structure allows individuals to communicate complex ideas effectively, building a bridge from intermediate conversation to advanced B2 fluency.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Extended Spontaneous Discourse & Debate Structure

content.summary: This briefing covers strategies for listening to extended spontaneous discourse, recognizing signposting language, and identifying how speakers structure complex arguments in academic debates.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of an extended academic debate conversation
Identify details such as thesis statements, counterarguments, and conclusions
Notice how words link together in connected speech during rapid discussions

keyPhrases.note: Used to introduce the central argument of a debate speech.
A point raised to oppose an opposing viewpoint or claim.
A question asked to make a point rather than get an answer.
A statement designed to urge an audience to take specific action.

connectedSpeech.note: Linking the final /t/ of start with with, and blending articles into the phrase.
Elision of the weak /ð/ sound in their when spoken quickly.
Assimilation of nasal /n/ to /ŋ/ and reduction of to into schwa.
Dropping unstressed vowels in professional for natural pacing.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Bridge to B2: Extended Spontaneous Discourse, Debate & Argument Structure

content.summary: Practical guide on organizing extended arguments, structuring debates, and using high-level discourse markers for B1 to B2 transition.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Opening Statement Structure
blueprintItems.formula: I believe/argue that [thesis]. I will discuss [point 1], [point 2], and [point 3].
blueprintItems.example: I argue that modern technology improves education. I will discuss accessibility, engagement, and flexibility.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: The PEE Framework
blueprintItems.example: Firstly, online learning increases accessibility. For instance, students can join classes from remote areas. This demonstrates that geographical barriers no longer block learning.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Counterarguments and Refutations
blueprintItems.formula: While some may argue that [counterargument], however [your refutation]. Moreover, [additional support].
blueprintItems.example: While some may argue that screens cause distraction, however students can learn self-discipline. Moreover, teachers can monitor digital focus easily.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use formal transition markers instead of simple connecting words like 'and' or 'so' when writing academic arguments.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Online classes are cheap and they are flexible, so many students like them.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Online classes are economical. Furthermore, they offer remarkable flexibility; consequently, many students prefer them.
mechanicsRules.why: B2 writing requires varied conjunctions and transitional adverbs to show logical relationships clearly.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always introduce counterarguments using concessive clauses before presenting your main refutation.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Some people think technology is bad. I think technology is good.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Although critics argue that digital tools reduce personal interaction, evidence shows virtual collaboration builds strong team skills.
mechanicsRules.why: Acknowledging opposing views makes your argumentative writing balanced and persuasive.

mechanicsRules.rule: Ensure pronoun reference is clear when linking complex multi-clause sentences.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Students use laptops and tablets during lessons because they help them.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Students use laptops and tablets during lessons because these devices enhance their productivity.
mechanicsRules.why: Using specific nouns instead of ambiguous pronouns prevents confusion in long sentences.

sampleSentences.en: Furthermore, research indicates that interactive learning boosts student retention rates significantly.
sampleSentences.id: Selain itu, penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran interaktif secara signifikan meningkatkan tingkat retensi siswa.

sampleSentences.en: Nevertheless, critics often highlight the potential negative impact of excessive screen time.
sampleSentences.id: Kendati demikian, para kritikus sering menyoroti potensi dampak negatif dari waktu layar yang berlebihan.

sampleSentences.en: In contrast to traditional classrooms, virtual learning environments offer personalized pacing.
sampleSentences.id: Berbeda dengan ruang kelas tradisional, lingkungan belajar virtual menawarkan kecepatan yang dipersonalisasi.

sampleSentences.en: Consequently, educational institutions must adapt their curricula to meet modern demands.
sampleSentences.id: Akibatnya, lembaga pendidikan harus menyesuaikan kurikulum mereka untuk memenuhi tuntutan modern.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: furthermore some people argues that online learning is bad
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Furthermore, some people argue that online learning is bad.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Selain itu, beberapa orang berpendapat bahwa pembelajaran online itu buruk.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize the first letter of a sentence, add a comma after introductory transition markers, and use plural verb agreement with 'people'.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: nevertheless traditional schools provides better social skills
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Nevertheless, traditional schools provide better social skills.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Kendati demikian, sekolah tradisional memberikan keterampilan sosial yang lebih baik.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use a comma after introductory transition words and match plural subject 'schools' with base verb 'provide'.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: in contrast to this view digital tools improves productivity
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: In contrast to this view, digital tools improve productivity.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Berbeda dengan pandangan ini, alat digital meningkatkan produktivitas.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Place a comma after introductory prepositional phrases and use plural verb 'improve' for plural subject 'tools'.

sentenceBuilderTargets.fullSentence: I argue that technology improves education.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Write an Opening Statement
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write an opening paragraph for a debate about homework. State your thesis clearly and preview two main points using the formula learned in theory.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I argue that excessive homework harms student well-being. I will discuss stress levels and lack of free time.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Construct a PEE Paragraph
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph supporting a point about learning languages online using the Point, Evidence, Explanation framework.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Firstly, online language apps increase daily practice. For instance, learners can complete five-minute exercises during their commute. This demonstrates that busy schedules no longer prevent language acquisition.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following simple sentence into an argument opening using 'I argue that':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Artificial intelligence helps modern students learn faster.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'I argue that' followed by the original clause.
targetAnswers: I argue that artificial intelligence helps modern students learn faster.
I argue that Artificial intelligence helps modern students learn faster.
practicumQuestions.explanation: An argument opening clearly states your stance using introductory phrases like 'I argue that'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct discourse marker for addition: 'Online courses are flexible. _______, they are often more affordable.'
practicumQuestions.promptText: Online courses are flexible. [blank], they are often more affordable.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a formal transition word meaning 'in addition'.
targetAnswers: Furthermore
Furthermore,
Moreover
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Furthermore' or 'Moreover' adds supporting points effectively in academic discourse.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct all capitalization and punctuation errors in the following sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: nevertheless some experts disagree with this conclusion
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word and add a comma after the transition marker.
targetAnswers: Nevertheless, some experts disagree with this conclusion.
Nevertheless, some experts disagree with this conclusion
practicumQuestions.explanation: Introductory transition markers like 'Nevertheless' require a comma and a capital letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete PEE 'Point' sentence arguing that reading books improves vocabulary.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Firstly,' or state your point directly.
targetAnswers: Firstly, reading books regularly expands a student's active vocabulary.
Firstly, reading books expands vocabulary.
Reading books improves vocabulary by exposing learners to new words.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A strong PEE point is clear, concise, and directly addresses the topic.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using a contrastive transition marker ('In contrast'):
practicumQuestions.promptText: Traditional classrooms require physical presence. Online classes offer location freedom.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin the second sentence with 'In contrast,'.
targetAnswers: Traditional classrooms require physical presence. In contrast, online classes offer location freedom.
Traditional classrooms require physical presence; in contrast, online classes offer location freedom.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'In contrast' highlights clear differences between two subjects.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Choose the correct resultative transition word: 'Students practiced every day; _______, their speaking fluency improved rapidly.'
practicumQuestions.promptText: Students practiced every day; [blank], their speaking fluency improved rapidly.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a word meaning 'as a result'.
targetAnswers: consequently
Consequently
therefore
Therefore
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Consequently' and 'therefore' show clear cause and effect relationships.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Identify and correct the subject-verb agreement error in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Every student in the debate team have prepared their arguments.
targetAnswers: Every student in the debate team has prepared their arguments.
Every student in the debate team has prepared his or her arguments.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Every student' is singular and requires the singular verb 'has'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a counterargument sentence acknowledging that uniforms save time.
targetAnswers: While some may argue that school uniforms save time in the morning, others feel they restrict personal expression.
While some may argue that uniforms save time, they reduce individuality.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Concessive clauses beginning with 'While some may argue' successfully introduce opposing views.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine these two sentences using 'Because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Extended discourse builds speaking confidence. Students should practice daily.
practicumQuestions.hint: Place 'Because' at the beginning or connect with a comma.
targetAnswers: Because extended discourse builds speaking confidence, students should practice daily.
Students should practice daily because extended discourse builds speaking confidence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Subordinating conjunctions like 'because' link causes to main clauses smoothly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a concluding summary sentence using 'In conclusion'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Topic: The value of debate practice.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'In conclusion,' and restate the main benefit.
targetAnswers: In conclusion, debate practice develops critical thinking and persuasive communication skills.
In conclusion, structured debates improve overall speaking competence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A powerful conclusion restates the thesis and synthesizes the main arguments.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Bridge to B2: Extended Spontaneous Discourse, Debate & Argument Structure

content.summary: This module prepares you for B2 level speaking by focusing on extended spontaneous discourse, structuring complex arguments, and delivering persuasive speeches. You will learn how to connect ideas smoothly using advanced transition markers and counterarguments.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to sentence stress and intonation when presenting counterarguments. Use falling intonation to state firm claims and rising intonation when introducing contrasting viewpoints.

pillars.name: Discourse Markers
pillars.explanation: Use linking words like furthermore, nevertheless, and consequently to guide your listener through multi-point arguments.

pillars.name: Argument Structure
pillars.target: Clear thesis, supporting points, and synthesis
pillars.explanation: State your stance clearly, provide a compelling reason, acknowledge an opposing view, and conclude with a strong synthesis.

pillars.name: Vocal Projection
pillars.target: Controlled volume and pacing for debate
pillars.explanation: Maintain an even speaking pace without excessive filler words such as um or ah to sound confident and authoritative.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress shifts depending on the word length and grammatical category.
The stress remains firmly on the second syllable in both words during debate phrasing.
Strong stress falls on the final syllable of verbs like refute.
Three-syllable verbs and nouns place primary stress on the first syllable.

drills.targetText: Furthermore, the research indicates that regular exercise improves mental health.
drills.phonetic: /ˌfɜːðəˈmɔːr ðə rɪˈsɜːtʃ ˈɪndɪkeɪts ðæt ˈreɡjʊlə ˈeksəsaɪz ɪmˈpruːvz ˈmentəl helθ/
drills.focus: Advanced transition marker 'Furthermore' and clear clause pausing
drills.hint: Pause briefly after 'Furthermore' to let your main argument land.

drills.targetText: Nevertheless, I believe we should proceed with caution.
drills.phonetic: /ˌnevəðəˈles aɪ bɪˈliːv wiː ʃʊd prəˈsiːd wɪð ˈkɔːʃən/
drills.hint: Emphasize 'Nevertheless' to show you are introducing a counterpoint.

drills.targetText: A common counterargument is that technology reduces face-to-face communication.
drills.phonetic: /ə ˈkɒmən ˈkaʊntərˌɑːrɡjəmənt ɪz ðæt tekˈnɒlədʒi rɪˈduːsɪz feɪs tuː feɪs kəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃən/
drills.hint: Keep your voice steady through 'face-to-face' without awkward pauses.

drills.targetText: She presented compelling evidence that supports her position.
drills.phonetic: /ʃiː prɪˈzentɪd kəmˈpelɪŋ ˈevɪdəns ðæt səˈpɔːts hɜːr pəˈzɪʃən/
drills.focus: Adjective-noun stress balance in debate vocabulary
drills.hint: Stress the second syllable of 'compelling' strongly.

roleplay.context: You are participating in a formal school debate club meeting discussing modern technology.

turns.speaker: Debate Moderator
turns.text: What is your primary stance on whether online learning replaces traditional classrooms?
turns.translation: Apa pendirian utamamu mengenai apakah pembelajaran online menggantikan kelas tradisional?

turns.speaker: Student Speaker
turns.text: I advocate for a hybrid model because online tools offer flexibility, nevertheless physical presence remains essential.
turns.translation: Saya mendukung model hibrida karena alat online menawarkan fleksibilitas, namun kehadiran fisik tetap penting.

turns.speaker: Debate Moderator
turns.text: How do you respond to the counterargument that digital distraction ruins concentration?
turns.translation: Bagaimana kamu menanggapi argumen tandingan bahwa gangguan digital merusak konsentrasi?

turns.speaker: Student Speaker
turns.text: I acknowledge that distraction is a risk, but students can learn self-discipline, and consequently improve their focus over time.
turns.translation: Saya mengakui bahwa gangguan adalah risiko, tetapi siswa dapat belajar disiplin diri, dan akibatnya meningkatkan fokus mereka seiring waktu.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a memorable debate or discussion you had recently.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about a time you had to defend your opinion against someone who disagreed with you.
storyPoints: What topic or issue was being discussed
What your main argument was and how you presented it
How the discussion ended and what you learned from it
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Last week I discussed renewable energy, presented compelling facts, and reached a clear agreement.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /lɑːst wiːk aɪ dɪˈskʌst rɪˈnjuːəbəl ˈenədʒi prɪˈzentɪd kəmˈpelɪŋ fækts/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Speak fluently in full sentences using past tense narrative structures.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about your future academic or career goals.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe what you plan to study or achieve in the next five years and why.
storyPoints: Your main career or academic ambition
Why you advocate for this specific field of study
The steps you will take to reach your goal successfully
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I advocate for environmental science studies because I want to protect our natural resources.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ ˈædvəkeɪt fɔːr ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentəl ˈsaɪəns ˈstʌdiz bɪˈkɒz aɪ wɒnt tuː prəˈtekt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use present simple and future intentions with smooth pacing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the moderator's question about public speaking in professional environments.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Why do you think discourse analysis and public speaking skills matter in modern careers?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are being interviewed by a hiring manager for an internship position.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Furthermore, effective discourse helps teams communicate clearly and solve complex problems.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌfɜːðəˈmɔːr ɪˈfektɪv ˈdɪskɔːrs helps tiːmz kəˈmjuːnɪkeɪt ˈklɪəli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Deliver your response with a professional tone and confident pacing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Address the challenge raised by your colleague during a project meeting.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your colleague says the new marketing plan is too risky. How do you reply?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are leading a marketing strategy meeting with your team.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I acknowledge your concern, nevertheless our research shows compelling market demand.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ əkˈnɒlɪdʒ jɔːr kənˈsɜːn ˌnevəðəˈles ˈaʊə rɪˈsɜːtʃ ʃəʊz kəmˈpelɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Balance diplomatic phrasing with a firm argumentative stance.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Refute an opposing claim during a formal academic seminar.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Someone argues that artificial intelligence will destroy jobs. How do you refute this?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are presenting a paper at a university student conference.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I must refute that claim because technology creates new roles while replacing routine tasks.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ mʌst rɪˈfjuːt ðæt kleɪm bɪˈkɒz tekˈnɒlədʒi kriːeɪts nuː rəʊlz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use crisp articulation and firm stress on the verb refute.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Synthesize the main points at the end of a group discussion.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Can you summarize what our group has agreed upon regarding the school budget?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are wrapping up a student council budget allocation meeting.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: To synthesize our discussion, we will allocate funds to library upgrades and sports equipment.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /tuː ˈsɪnθəsaɪz ˈaʊə dɪˈskʌʃən wiː wɪl ˈæləkeɪt fʌndz tuː ˈlaɪbrəri/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Speak clearly with a concluding tone to show resolution.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence aloud using the target vocabulary word correctly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence: The committee decided to synthesize all reports into one document.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The committee decided to synthesize all reports into one document.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə kəˈmɪti dɪˈsaɪdɪd tuː ˈsɪnθəsaɪz ɔːl rɪˈpɔːts ˈɪntuː wʌn ˈdɒkjʊmənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ensure accurate pronunciation of the verb synthesize with stress on the first syllable.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the complex conditional sentence aloud with proper clause linking.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence: Had we invested earlier, we would have avoided these financial consequences.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Had we invested earlier, we would have avoided these financial consequences.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hæd wiː ɪnˈvestɪd ˈɜːliə wiː wʊd həv əˈvɔɪdɪd ðiːz fəˈnænʃəl ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maintain a natural rhythm through the inverted conditional clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence focusing on correct syllable stress in multisyllabic words.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence: The counterargument provided compelling evidence for the debate.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The counterargument provided compelling evidence for the debate.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈkaʊntərˌɑːrɡjəmənt prəˈvaɪdɪd kəmˈpelɪŋ ˈevɪdəns fɔːr ðə dɪˈbeɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Place primary stress correctly on counterargument and compelling.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice contrastive intonation using rising tone for the clause and falling tone for the conclusion.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence: Although the task was challenging, consequently our team succeeded brilliantly.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Although the task was challenging, consequently our team succeeded brilliantly.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɔːlˈðəʊ ðə tɑːsk wɒz ˈtʃælɪndʒɪŋ ˈkɒnsɪkwəntli ˈaʊə tiːm səkˈsiːdɪd ˈbrɪliəntli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a rising pitch on challenging to show contrast, followed by a falling pitch on brilliantly.
